subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox prune does not clean up workspace directory

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the conflicting linked fork fix for this focused workspace-prune bug, or fold the cleanup into the broader managed sandbox lifecycle issue?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but workspace deletion can remove user/session state and the open fork PR plus broader lifecycle issue make the implementation route an ownership choice.

options.title: Adopt a narrow safe cleanup
options.body: Replace or update the linked fix with a current-main patch that deletes only eligible non-shared sandbox-owned workspaces after successful runtime removal and adds focused regression tests.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle work
options.body: Keep this issue open as supporting context while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98516 defines the broader owner-scoped cleanup policy.

options.title: Resolve the fork PR first
options.body: Close, rebase, or supersede the conflicting fork PR before allowing another automated repair path so there is one canonical implementation target.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow safe cleanup
recommendation.body: Replace or update the linked fix with a current-main patch that deletes only eligible non-shared sandbox-owned workspaces after successful runtime removal and adds focused regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history on sandbox lifecycle, prune, and backend ownership and authored the broader lifecycle issue that overlaps this cleanup.
